title: Do people trust China, the U.S. or the EU to regulate AI?
summary: Trust in China, the U.S. and the EU to regulate AI is tied to overall favorability. Many people trust their own country more than any other regulator.

title: Appendix: Detailed tables
Concerns about AI are especially widespread in high-income countries
summary: People in high-income countries are more likely than those in less wealthy nations to be concerned about AI, as well as its impact on jobs and economic inequality.

title: Who has heard or read a lot about AI, and how is awareness changing?
summary: Majorities in most of 37 countries surveyed have at least some awareness of AI. In some places, the share who has heard a lot about it has increased since last year.

title: What do young people around the world think about AI?
summary: A 37-country survey finds that young adults are particularly worried about AI leading to fewer jobs. Still, they're more likely than older people to feel both excited and concerned about AI.

title: Globally, More People Expect AI to Cause Job Loss Than Growth
summary: Amid a mix of concern and excitement about AI, a 37-country survey finds pessimism about its potential impact on jobs and economic inequality.

title: Democrats are now more worried than Republicans about AI and its impact on jobs
summary: In another shift, Democrats are now more likely than Republicans to predict that AI will lead to fewer jobs over the next 20 years (75% vs. 68%).

title: Survey panels can make political party affiliation weighting easier
summary: One challenge pollsters face when weighting surveys based on people’s self-reported political party affiliation is that the population target can change fairly quickly. One year, Americans may be evenly divided between Republicans and Democrats. The next year, politics may shift and one party clearly outnumbers the other in supporters. title: Why many polls need to weight on party affiliation or past vote

summary: There are good arguments against weighting surveys to match how people voted in past elections or an independent estimate of political party affiliation. title: About 9 in 10 Palestinians in the West Bank and East Jerusalem see Israeli checkpoints as a major problem
summary: A large majority of Palestinians in the West Bank and East Jerusalem (85%) also say that opportunities for work are a major problem for them and their families.

title: Who is Hispanic?
summary: More than 70 million people in the U.S. identify as Hispanic today, but government agencies and survey organizations don't count the Hispanic population in the same way.

title: Americans Value Press Freedom but Differ on Its Limits
summary: Many people in the U.S. say some press freedom restrictions are OK when weighed against concerns about false information or national security.

title: How much do Americans know about the First Amendment?
summary: About half of U.S. adults correctly identified that the First Amendment guarantees freedom of the press.
